newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga Kristin find shows 700 mln boe.
newsitem.headline: Saga Kristin find shows 700 mln boe.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday the first well on its Kristin gas and condensate discovery in the Haltenbanken in the Norwegian Sea confirmed reserves of about 700 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).
The company said the well proved the reserves were 60 percent gas and 40 percent condensate.
In a statement Saga said the find could contain even more hydrocarbons.
"Block 6506/2, in which both the Kristin and Lavrans discoveries lie, will be Saga's main challenge during the next five years," the company's statement said.
"Each of these discoveries...appears to be larger than any other discovery made on the Norwegian shelf during the last 10 years."
Saga said its exploration activity would increase strongly in 1997 and exploration costs are expected to double compared with previous years.

Norway's largest listed oil company said it planned to spend 700 million crowns on the Norwegian continental shelf and and a further 300 million crowns on international exploration -- mainly in British waters.
